ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A worker with a mass of $m = 60\,\mathrm{kg}$ is wearing a safety harness with an original length of $L = 5\,\mathrm{m}$ while working at height. If the worker accidentally falls, the time from when the safety harness begins to tighten to its maximum extension is $t = 1\,\mathrm{s}$. Treat the worker as a point mass and neglect air resistance during the fall. Take $g = 10\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. From the moment of falling until the safety belt begins to tighten, the magnitude of the worker's velocity $v$.
2. During the process of falling until the safety belt reaches its maximum length, the magnitude of the impulse $I$ due to gravity acting on the worker.
3. During the process from initial tension to the longest state, the magnitude of the average impulsive force $F$ experienced by the seat belt.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, it can be seen that a worker is on a high platform, and the safety belt/rope is in a slack state, hanging downward from near the platform, with the length L marked beside it using a vertical double-headed arrow. This indicates that after the worker falls, he first passes through a vertical distance L before the safety belt begins to tighten. Reasoning: The problem gives m = 60 kg, L = 5 m, g = 10 m/s^2, and the time from when the safety belt begins to tighten to when it reaches maximum elongation is t = 1 s. 1. Before the safety belt tightens, the worker freely falls through the distance L, so v^2 = 2gL. Substituting gives v = sqrt(2 × 10 × 5) = 10 m/s. 2. The time used in the free-fall stage is t_free = v/g = 10/10 = 1 s. From the beginning of the fall to when the safety belt reaches maximum elongation, the total time is t_free + t = 1 + 1 = 2 s. The magnitude of the impulse of gravity is I_g = mg(t_free + t) = 60 × 10 × 2 = 1200 N·s. 3. During the 1 s from when the safety belt has just tightened to when it is longest, take vertically downward as positive. The initial momentum is mv = 60 × 10 = 600 kg·m/s, and when maximum elongation is reached, the velocity is instantaneously 0, so the final momentum is 0, and therefore the change in momentum is -600 kg·m/s. The impulse of gravity in this stage is mg t = 60 × 10 × 1 = 600 N·s. The average force exerted by the safety belt on the person is upward, with magnitude F, so the impulse equation is mg t - F t = -mv. Substituting gives 600 - F × 1 = -600, so F = 1200 N. The average impact force exerted on the safety belt by the worker has the same magnitude, 1200 N.
